## FeNyx : Ember

Crovan is now FeNyx: a cleaner, darker look, two new mode names — Jarvis for your phone and Friday for classroom smart panels — and big files that no longer crash.

### ✨ What's New

- 🔵 **Jarvis : Phone mode** — Your phone. Send (Transmit) and receive (Retrieve), switch with the round buttons or swipe.
- 🟠 **Friday : Panel mode** — Turns a tablet or smart panel into a file drop with a large, self-refreshing QR code.
- 💡 **Mode light** — A small glowing light beside the title shows the mode (🔵 Jarvis / 🟠 Friday). Hold it to switch; a short black-screen intro confirms the change. Tap to skip.
- ⭕ **Progress ring** — Transfers show a ring that fills up and turns red → yellow → green, with speed, amount sent and time left.
- 📦 **Big files fixed** — 10 GB and larger files now send without the app closing. FeNyx also checks free space before saving.
- 🔘 **New buttons** — Round glass buttons at the bottom replace the old text buttons. Cancel, Done and Retry are round too.
- 🚀 **Finish animation** — The suit flies off after sending and lands after receiving. Tap to skip, or turn off Full effects in Settings.
- 🔤 **New fonts** — Inter for text and JetBrains Mono for codes, so codes are easier to read out.
- 🎨 **New name and icon** — Crovan becomes FeNyx, with the red and gold arrows icon and an Android themed icon.

### 📥 Two Versions

- **Standard** (about 16 MB) — works with both old and new croc. Pick this if unsure.
- **Lite** (about 12 MB) — newest croc only, smaller download.

Both look and work the same, and either installs over the other.

### ⚠️ Important — Before You Install

FeNyx has a new app ID, so it installs next to Crovan instead of replacing it.

- **Coming from Crovan:** install FeNyx, then uninstall Crovan when you no longer need its history. History and settings do not carry over.
- Received files are now saved in `Downloads/FeNyx`.
- Needs Android 8 or newer on a 64-bit phone.

### 📦 Based On

FeNyx (formerly Crovan and Kroc-Sauria) is a fork of Croc by schollz.
The underlying Croc project and its original authors remain credited.
